history.text: Old cores collide and weld into the First Land; their seams become the inland belts of the Eastern, Northern and Southern continents and the old core under Garyk.
The First Land rifts apart around Garyk; the rifts become passive, smooth coasts with wide shelves.
The pieces drift to where they stand today, each turning about its own pole.
Leading edges override sinking sea floor: coastal ranges, volcanoes and island arcs grow along them.
The Northern Garyk Sea Plate closes on Garyk; its northern ranges rise along the seam.
Wear and the slow rebound of the crust soften the old belts to rounded hills and lower the young ranges.
Caren is set down whole by the gods into the sea where the First Land had broken apart. It takes no part in the turning of the plates.

caren.summary: Caren is the Godstone: a single block laid down by the gods and their angels, not raised by the turning of the plates. It has no fault, no volcano and no rift, and it does not drift with the plate it rests on.

rocks.note: fine, even, almost without seams; it does not weather into tors
banded white and grey; the classic building stone
thin, fertile, with springs where it meets the granite

caren.earthquakes: none: the Godstone does not move; tremors from the sea floor around it are felt only faintly on its coasts

garyk.core: old core of granite and gneiss under the interior (part of the First Land)
